seo.description: 20 High-yield JEE Main MCQ practice questions covering Free Body Diagrams (FBD), Atwood machines, contact forces between touching blocks, wedge-block pseudo-acceleration, and heavy rope tension distributions.

conceptCapsule.title: Systematic Construction of Free Body Diagrams & Constraint Equations
conceptCapsule.summary:
1. FBD Principle: Isolate the body of interest and represent all external real forces acting directly on it (field forces like gravity $m\vec{g}$, contact normal forces $\vec{N}$, string tensions $\vec{T}$, and friction $\vec{f}$).
 2. Connected Systems: For blocks connected by taut, massless, inextensible strings over ideal pulleys: $a = \frac{\sum F_{\text{driving}}}{\sum M_{\text{total}}}$. 
In an Atwood machine: $a = \frac{(m_1 - m_2)g}{m_1 + m_2}$, $T = \frac{2m_1 m_2 g}{m_1 + m_2}$, reaction on pulley hinge $R_p = 2T$. 
3. Wedge-Block Constraints: To prevent a block from sliding on a smooth incline of angle $\theta$, horizontal wedge acceleration must be $a = g\tan\theta$ (into the incline), giving normal force $N = \frac{mg}{\cos\theta}$.
conceptCapsule.keyFormula: $$a = \frac{(m_1 - m_2)g}{m_1 + m_2}, \quad T = \frac{2m_1 m_2 g}{m_1 + m_2}, \quad a_{\text{table}} = \frac{m_2 g}{m_1 + m_2}, \quad a_{\text{wedge}} = g\tan\theta, \quad N_{\text{wedge}} = \frac{mg}{\cos\theta}$$
conceptCapsule.examTrap: Do not include internal forces when considering an isolated body's FBD. When analyzing heavy ropes of mass $m$ pulling mass $M$ with force $F$, tension is not uniform: tension at distance $x$ from the pulled end is $T(x) = F\left(1 - \frac{mx}{(M+m)L}\right)$. For falling chains, the total normal force on the table at fallen length $x$ is $N = 3\left(\frac{M}{L}\right)gx$ (1 part static weight $+$ 2 parts dynamic impact momentum rate).

questions.statement: In a standard Atwood machine, two masses $m_1 = 3\text{ kg}$ and $m_2 = 2\text{ kg}$ are connected by a light, inextensible string passing over a frictionless, massless pulley. The acceleration of the system is: (Take $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$)
questions.solution:
$$a = \frac{(m_1 - m_2)g}{m_1 + m_2} = \frac{(3 - 2) \times 10}{3 + 2} = \frac{10}{5} = 2.0\text{ m/s}^2$$
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: In the Atwood machine described in Q1, the tension in the string connecting the two masses is:
questions.solution:
$$T = \frac{2m_1 m_2 g}{m_1 + m_2} = \frac{2 \times 3 \times 2 \times 10}{3 + 2} = \frac{120}{5} = 24\text{ N}$$
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: In Q1, the total downward reaction force exerted by the string on the pulley axle is:
questions.solution:
The pulley supports two vertical segments of string carrying tension $T = 24\text{ N}$: $$R_{\text{pulley}} = 2T = 2 \times 24 = 48\text{ N}$$
Therefore, Option D is correct.

questions.statement: A block of mass $m_1 = 4\text{ kg}$ rests on a smooth horizontal table and is connected by a light string passing over a frictionless pulley at the table edge to a hanging block of mass $m_2 = 6\text{ kg}$. The acceleration of the system is: (Take $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$)
questions.solution:
$$a = \frac{m_2 g}{m_1 + m_2} = \frac{6 \times 10}{4 + 6} = \frac{60}{10} = 6.0\text{ m/s}^2$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: In the system of Q4, the tension in the connecting string is:
questions.solution:
Tension accelerates block $m_1$: $$T = m_1 a = 4 \times 6.0 = 24\text{ N}$$
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: Three blocks of masses $m_1 = 1\text{ kg}$, $m_2 = 2\text{ kg}$, and $m_3 = 3\text{ kg}$ are in contact on a smooth horizontal surface. A horizontal force $F = 18\text{ N}$ is applied to $m_1$ towards $m_3$. The contact force between $m_2$ and $m_3$ is:
questions.solution:
1. Acceleration $a = \frac{F}{m_1 + m_2 + m_3} = \frac{18}{1 + 2 + 3} = 3\text{ m/s}^2$.
2. Contact force $N_{23}$ accelerates block $m_3$: $N_{23} = m_3 a = 3 \times 3 = 9\text{ N}$.
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: A block of mass $M$ is pulled along a frictionless horizontal surface by a uniform heavy rope of mass $m$ using a horizontal force $F$ applied at the free end of the rope. The tension at the midpoint of the rope is:
questions.solution:
1. Acceleration $a = \frac{F}{M + m}$.
2. The midpoint of the rope pulls mass behind it $(M + m/2)$: $$T_{\text{mid}} = \left(M + \frac{m}{2}\right)a = \frac{(M + m/2)F}{M + m}$$
Therefore, Option D is correct.

questions.statement: A monkey of mass $m = 40\text{ kg}$ climbs up a vertical light rope which can withstand a maximum tension of $T_{\max} = 600\text{ N}$. The maximum acceleration with which the monkey can safely climb up is: (Take $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$)
questions.solution:
$$T - mg = ma \implies a_{\max} = \frac{T_{\max} - mg}{m} = \frac{600 - 400}{40} = 5.0\text{ m/s}^2$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: A block of mass $m = 5\text{ kg}$ is kept on a smooth inclined plane of inclination $\theta = 30^\circ$. The block is connected to a light string passing over a smooth pulley at the top of the incline supporting a hanging mass $M$. For the system to remain in static equilibrium, the mass $M$ must be:
questions.solution:
Equating string tensions: $$Mg = mg\sin(30^\circ) \implies M = 5 \times 0.5 = 2.5\text{ kg}$$
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: In a movable pulley system, a block of mass $M$ is supported by a movable pulley. A person pulls the free end of the string with force $F$. The acceleration of the block $M$ upward in terms of $F, M,$ and $g$ is: (Assume massless, frictionless pulley)
questions.solution:
The movable pulley provides two upward string segments with tension $F$. Net force on mass $M$: $$\sum F = 2F - Mg = Ma \implies a = \frac{2F}{M} - g$$
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: A painter of mass $M = 60\text{ kg}$ stands in a cradle of mass $m = 20\text{ kg}$ and pulls himself up with a light rope passing over a fixed smooth overhead pulley. To ascend with an acceleration $a = 2\text{ m/s}^2$, the force with which he must pull the rope is: (Take $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$)
questions.solution:
Two rope segments support the combined system $(M + m)$: $$2F - (M + m)g = (M + m)a \implies 2F - 800 = 80(2) = 160 \implies 2F = 960 \implies F = 480\text{ N}$$
Therefore, Option D is correct.

questions.statement: In Q11, the normal contact force exerted by the painter on the floor of the cradle is:
questions.solution:
FBD of painter: upward forces $N + F$, downward force $Mg$: $$N + F - Mg = Ma \implies N + 480 - 600 = 60(2) = 120 \implies N = 240\text{ N}$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: Two masses $m_1 = 5\text{ kg}$ and $m_2 = 10\text{ kg}$ are connected by a light string on a double inclined plane with inclinations $\theta_1 = 30^\circ$ and $\theta_2 = 60^\circ$ over a smooth apex pulley. The acceleration of mass $m_2$ down the plane is: (Take $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$)
questions.solution:
1. Net driving force: $F_{\text{net}} = m_2 g\sin 60^\circ - m_1 g\sin 30^\circ = 10(10)\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} - 5(10)(0.5) = 50\sqrt{3} - 25\text{ N}$.
2. Total mass: $M = 15\text{ kg}$.
3. $a = \frac{50\sqrt{3} - 25}{15} = \frac{5(2\sqrt{3}-1)}{3} \approx 4.11\text{ m/s}^2$.
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: A block of mass $m = 2\text{ kg}$ is suspended by two light strings making angles $\theta_1 = 30^\circ$ and $\theta_2 = 60^\circ$ with the horizontal ceiling. The tensions $T_1$ and $T_2$ in the strings are: (Take $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$)
questions.solution:
1. Horizontal: $T_1\cos 30^\circ = T_2\cos 60^\circ \implies T_2 = \sqrt{3}T_1$.
2. Vertical: $T_1\sin 30^\circ + T_2\sin 60^\circ = 20 \implies \frac{1}{2}T_1 + \frac{3}{2}T_1 = 20 \implies 2T_1 = 20 \implies T_1 = 10\text{ N}, T_2 = 10\sqrt{3}\text{ N}$.
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: In a wedge-block system, a block of mass $m$ is placed on a smooth wedge of inclination $\theta$. To keep the block stationary relative to the wedge, the horizontal acceleration $a$ given to the wedge must be:
questions.solution:
In wedge frame (pseudo-force $ma$ rightward): $$mg\sin\theta = ma\cos\theta \implies a = g\tan\theta\text{ (towards left)}$$
Therefore, Option D is correct.

questions.statement: In the previous question, the normal force exerted by the wedge on the block during this accelerated motion is:
questions.solution:
$$N = mg\cos\theta + ma\sin\theta = mg\left(\cos\theta + \frac{\sin^2\theta}{\cos\theta}\right) = \frac{mg}{\cos\theta}$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: A block $A$ of mass $m$ is attached to a light spring of stiffness $k$, which is connected to a block $B$ of mass $2m$. The system is placed on a frictionless table. If block $A$ is pulled with acceleration $a_0$, the acceleration of block $B$ at that exact instant is:
questions.solution:
At $t = 0$, spring extension $\Delta x = 0$, so spring force on block $B$ is $F_s = k\Delta x = 0$. Thus, $a_B = 0$.
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: A chain of length $L$ and mass $M$ is held vertically with its lower end touching a table. If it is released from rest, the force exerted by the chain on the table when a length $x$ has fallen is:
questions.solution:
1. Static weight of fallen chain: $W = \left(\frac{M}{L}x\right)g$.
2. Rate of momentum destruction: $F_v = v\frac{dm}{dt} = v\left(\frac{M}{L}v\right) = \frac{M}{L}v^2 = \frac{M}{L}(2gx) = \frac{2Mgx}{L}$.
3. Total normal force: $N = W + F_v = \frac{3Mgx}{L}$.
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: In a pulley-block system, block $A$ moves downwards with speed $v_A$. If the string is looped around a movable pulley attached to block $B$, the constraint relation yields the upward velocity $v_B$ as:
questions.solution:
String length constraint: $x_A + 2x_B = \text{constant} \implies \dot{x}_A + 2\dot{x}_B = 0 \implies v_B = \frac{v_A}{2}$.
Therefore, Option D is correct.

questions.statement: A sphere of mass $M$ is held between a vertical wall and an inclined plane of inclination $	heta = 60^\circ$ with the horizontal. Assuming all surfaces are smooth, the normal force exerted by the vertical wall on the sphere is:
questions.solution:
1. Vertical balance: $N_i\sin 60^\circ = Mg \implies N_i = \frac{2Mg}{\sqrt{3}}$.
2. Horizontal balance: $N_w = N_i\cos 60^\circ = \left(\frac{2Mg}{\sqrt{3}}\right)\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) = \frac{Mg}{\sqrt{3}}$.
Therefore, Option A is correct.
